title: Principality of Iberia
capsule: The Principality of Iberia (ქართლის საერისმთავრო, kartlis saerismtavro) was the presiding-prince polity of Kartli in eastern Georgia. During the years 682–741 it was held by the Guaramid dynasty — Guaram II (c. 684–693) and Guaram III (c. 693–c. 748) — after the Chosroid princes were stripped of power for their failed revolt against Umayyad hegemony in the 680s. The presiding princes (eristavi/mtavari) balanced Umayyad Arab overlordship against Byzantium, several of them bearing the Byzantine court dignity of curopalates, while Khazar incursions threatened from the north. By the 730s Arab pressure intensified and a Muslim emir was installed at Tbilisi, culminating in the devastating campaign of Marwan ibn Muhammad ('Marwan the Deaf').
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. The core territory of Kartli is well-established, but the principality's fluctuating boundaries under Arab suzerainty between 682 and 741 are incompletely attested.
